label: Bible Study
prompt: Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be _____, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.
verse: Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.
note: Discipline doesn't feel joyous at the time — the fruit comes afterward.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Because thy lovingkindness is better than _____, my lips shall praise thee.
verse: Because thy lovingkindness is better than life, my lips shall praise thee.
note: Written in the wilderness of Judah: God's lovingkindness is better than life itself.

label: Sunday School
prompt: Took branches of _____ trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.
verse: Took branches of palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.
note: Palm Sunday gets its name from this verse — only John says the crowd's branches came from palm trees.

label: Deep Water
prompt: I made a _____ with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?
verse: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?
note: Job's defense of his integrity starts with a deal he made with his own eyes.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: That which the _____ hath left hath the locust eaten; and that which the locust hath left hath the cankerworm eaten; and that which the cankerworm hath left hath the caterpiller eaten.
verse: That which the palmerworm hath left hath the locust eaten; and that which the locust hath left hath the cankerworm eaten; and that which the cankerworm hath left hath the caterpiller eaten.
note: Joel's plague comes in four waves — palmerworm, locust, cankerworm, caterpiller — and the KJV spells that last one oddly too.
